title: The Python tooling standard is written from the kb's own practice
goal: kb/_self/code.md states the tooling's rules as the code already follows them: standard library only at runtime, portability (utf-8, newline, pathlib, argv subprocesses), git environment isolation in tests, deterministic and converging output, the documented exit-code pattern per tool, a planted failure for every gate, flat-prefixed modules behind a CLI facade, import direction and underscore-private names; and a test fails when a helper module imports its facade or a module imports another module's underscore name
notes: Written from existing practice, not an outside style guide. Exit codes are documented per tool as they are; nothing is renumbered. The git-environment rule cites BG-q67lvp5b “The backlog tests re-initialise the real repository under a pre-push hook”, which lands in SP-z7a5c76b first. Packages under _tools/ are out: a _tools/tests/ package would also shadow _tools/tests.py.
